items.q: Fess William Royal Flush Orchestra came back under the direction of a musician from Louisville, Kentucky named Lockwood Lewis... Lockwood played alto sax and clarinet and was a very good showman and a loveable person.

ctx.x: I hated to see the Horace Henderson group leave the place at the end of February because I had enjoyed the competition between the two orchestras and so had they. It had been a new experience for me and it was different from the way we had competed with the Buffalodians because they were at one end of the hall and we were at the other end. But at the Savoy the two bands were next to each other and we were real friendly enemies which made the competition greater and the desire to blow stronger. Rex and I were…

Fess William Royal Flush Orchestra came back under the direction of a musician from Louisville, Kentucky named Lockwood Lewis, because Fess had been engaged to direct the pit band of the Regal Theatre in Chicago. We changed to the bandstand where Horace had been because Fess had always used the one we had been on. Lockwood played alto sax and clarinet and was a very good showman and a loveable person. Dickie Wells and quite a number of other Louisville musicians had come up under the guidance of Lockwood.

The Royal Flush Orchestra didn't jump like Horace so the sign announcing the different dances was not used anymore. But we continued to play the hard driving swing that we did against the Henderson boys because it was our style and we made the Hoppers really take off when we were on the stand.
